scenario_name: Phishing Attachment to SMB Lateral Movement
scenario_summary: A user opens a malicious Office attachment delivered by email. A macro launches PowerShell, which establishes registry run-key persistence, performs local/domain discovery, and reuses a captured account to move laterally to the file server over SMB, where data is staged and archived before a small exfiltration burst to an external host.

attack_timeline.narrative: yhar-even receives and saves an email attachment (Vendor_Statement_Update.docm) to the Outlook secure temp cache.
Vendor_Statement_Update.docm opens the attachment; Word renders it with macros enabled.

technique.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Visual Basic

attack_timeline.narrative: The macro (VBA, not independently logged) invokes powershell.exe as its child process.
Decoded script block shows a download-and-execute against static-assets-cache.net.
attack_timeline.pivot: ScriptBlockText domain -> DNS query -> network connection

attack_timeline.narrative: powershell.exe repeatedly reconnects to static-assets-cache.net (203.0.113.133) over HTTPS -- 28 beacon-interval connections.
attack_timeline.pivot: count of connections to 203.0.113.133 over time -> beacon pattern

technique.name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder

attack_timeline.narrative: A Run-key value 'WindowsUpdateHelper' is created pointing at a dropped executable in AppData.
attack_timeline.pivot: TargetObject Run-key name -> reappears on every logon

attack_timeline.narrative: Local system, network config and process enumeration via cmd.exe/systeminfo/tasklist children of powershell.exe.
'net user /domain' and 'net group "Domain Admins" /domain' enumerate domain accounts.
'nltest /dclist' and 'net view \\FS01' enumerate reachable domain systems.
'net.exe use \\FS01\ADMIN$ /user:BRIGHTFIELD\adm-mrogers *' explicitly supplies a previously-harvested domain account (adm-mrogers) rather than the victim's own credentials.
attack_timeline.pivot: TargetUserName=adm-mrogers carries into the lateral-movement logon

attack_timeline.narrative: A Type 3 (network) logon for adm-mrogers lands on FS01 from WKS01 (10.42.20.85).
attack_timeline.pivot: TargetLogonId 0xf33c9c ties subsequent FS01 process activity to this session

attack_timeline.narrative: The same session immediately accesses the ADMIN$ administrative share on FS01 -- the delivery path for the payload dropped moments later.
attack_timeline.pivot: ShareName=\\FS01\ADMIN$ confirms admin-share access, closing the delivery-path gap

attack_timeline.narrative: A short-lived service ('WindowsUpdateSvc') is installed on FS01 to execute commands with SYSTEM-equivalent rights.
robocopy mirrors 14 files from \\FS01\Finance$ into a Windows\Temp staging directory.
Collected files sit under C:\Windows\Temp\svc_stage pending archival.

technique.name: Archive Collected Data: Archive via Utility

attack_timeline.narrative: Compress-Archive builds sys_diag.zip from the staged directory.
The archive is uploaded to 203.0.113.133 over the same HTTPS channel used for C2 -- a single large-sentbyte session (~61 MB).
attack_timeline.pivot: sentbyte outlier on FortiGate session to 203.0.113.133

false_positives.name: After-hours bulk AD export by IT admin
false_positives.why_benign: Matches the documented quarterly AD-export script path (C:\Scripts\quarterly_export.ps1) and runs from adm-mrogers's account on the domain controller itself -- expected admin workflow, not attacker discovery.

false_positives.name: Legitimate RDP admin session to FS01
false_positives.why_benign: Source is an internal workstation IP (10.42.20.176) -- not the reserved 203.0.113.0/24 attacker-infra block -- with a short, single session and a matching 4634/4647 logoff shortly after.

false_positives.name: Expired cached credential lockout (mazoulay)
false_positives.spl: index=hunt_lab sourcetype=wineventlog:security:json EventCode=4625 host=wks04 | stats count by TargetUserName
false_positives.why_benign: All 6 failures and the eventual success come from the user's own registered workstation (WKS04) with no external or lateral IP involved -- a stale cached password, not a brute force.

false_positives.name: Adobe Acrobat updater installs a service
false_positives.why_benign: ImagePath points at Adobe's own signed update-service binary under Program Files, installed immediately after a user-initiated download in the same session -- routine patching, not attacker persistence.

false_positives.name: Excel macro workbook spawns cmd.exe to archive a report
false_positives.why_benign: The known internal 'Monthly_Report_Macro.xlsm' workbook always spawns a single short-lived cmd.exe to copy its own output into an Archive folder -- consistent filename, consistent parent, no network activity, no persistence.

false_positives.name: Off-hours outbound sync to contracted backup vendor
false_positives.spl: index=hunt_lab sourcetype=fortigate dstip="198.51.100.0/24" app="backup-sync" | stats sum(sentbyte) by dstip
false_positives.why_benign: Large, sustained overnight upload from FS01 to a single stable vendor IP with app='backup-sync' -- matches the nightly offsite backup window, not the short bursty pattern seen from the attacker-infra block (203.0.113.0/24).
